## `items`
Order line items. One row per unit sold (no quantity column): units = row count. Join to orders for dates/stores and to products for name, type and price. For any sales-by-product, product-mix or category-share question, use the line_sales measure here. Do NOT use products.price:sum from this model: it sums each distinct product's price once, not once per item sold.
**Columns (4):**

| name | type | description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| id | TEXT | — |
| order_id | TEXT | Order this line belongs to. |
| sku | TEXT | Product sold on this line. |
| unit_price | DOUBLE | Price of the product on this line, in dollars (products.price is stored in cents). Row-level, so summing it gives sales per item sold. |

**Measures (2):**

| name | formula | description |
| --- | --- | --- |

WITH __slayer_stage_sku_cost AS (
  SELECT
    _stage_inner."supplies.sku" AS "sku",
    _stage_inner."supplies.unit_cost_cents" AS "unit_cost_cents"
  FROM (
    SELECT
      supplies.sku AS "supplies.sku",
      SUM(supplies.cost) AS "supplies.unit_cost_cents"
    FROM supplies AS supplies
    GROUP BY
      supplies.sku
  ) AS _stage_inner
), _base_2 AS (
  SELECT
    items.sku AS "items.sku",
    COUNT(items.id) AS "items.units"
  FROM items AS items
  LEFT JOIN orders AS orders
    ON items.order_id = orders.id
  LEFT JOIN stores AS orders__stores
    ON orders.store_id = orders__stores.id
  WHERE
    orders__stores.name = 'Brooklyn'
    AND orders.ordered_at >= CAST('2025-01-01 00:00:00' AS TIMESTAMP)
    AND orders.ordered_at < CAST('2026-01-01 00:00:00' AS TIMESTAMP)
  GROUP BY
    items.sku
), _cm_items__unit_price_sum AS (
  SELECT
    items.sku AS "items.sku",
    CAST(SUM(CAST(products.price / 100.0 AS DOUBLE)) AS DOUBLE) AS "items.sales"
  FROM items AS items
  LEFT JOIN orders AS orders
    ON items.order_id = orders.id
  LEFT JOIN stores AS orders__stores
    ON orders.store_id = orders__stores.id
  LEFT JOIN products AS products
    ON items.sku = products.sku
  WHERE
    orders__stores.name = 'Brooklyn'
    AND orders.ordered_at >= CAST('2025-01-01 00:00:00' AS TIMESTAMP)
    AND orders.ordered_at < CAST('2026-01-01 00:00:00' AS TIMESTAMP)
  GROUP BY
    items.sku
), __slayer_stage_sku_units AS (
  SELECT
    _stage_inner."items.sku" AS "sku",
    _stage_inner."items.units" AS "units",
    _stage_inner."items.sales" AS "sales"
  FROM (
    SELECT
      _base_2."items.sku",
      _base_2."items.units",
      _cm_items__unit_price_sum."items.sales"
    FROM _base_2
    LEFT JOIN _cm_items__unit_price_sum
      ON _base_2."items.sku" IS NOT DISTINCT FROM _cm_items__unit_price_sum."items.sku"
  ) AS _stage_inner
), _base AS (
  SELECT
    CAST(SUM(sku_units.sales) AS DOUBLE) AS "sku_units.total_sales",
    SUM(sku_units.units) AS "sku_units.total_units"
  FROM __slayer_stage_sku_units AS sku_units
), _cm_sku_units__units_sku_cost_unit_cost_cents_sum AS (
  SELECT
    SUM(sku_units.units * sku_cost.unit_cost_cents) AS "sku_units.units_sku_cost_unit_cost_cents_sum"
  FROM __slayer_stage_sku_units AS sku_units
  LEFT JOIN __slayer_stage_sku_cost AS sku_cost
    ON sku_units.sku = sku_cost.sku
)
SELECT
  _cm_sku_units__units_sku_cost_unit_cost_cents_sum."sku_units.units_sku_cost_unit_cost_cents_sum" / 100.0 AS "sku_units.supply_cost",
  _base."sku_units.total_sales",
  _base."sku_units.total_units"
FROM _base
CROSS JOIN _cm_sku_units__units_sku_cost_unit_cost_cents_sum
LIMIT 21

args.message: In 2025, Brooklyn's supply cost was $260,822.55 against $1,263,176.00 of pre-tax product sales, which leaves a gross margin of about 79.35% (0.7935184408). To get the supply cost, I added up each product's per-unit supply cost from its components and multiplied it by the number of units Brooklyn sold (178,840 units in total). The sales figure is the sum of item prices, and it matches the store's pre-tax order totals for 2025 exactly.
